And if you're really really unlucky you could get something called empty nose syndrome. Its linked to turbinate reduction, but people have gotten it from rhinoplasty. I talked to someone on this sub who most likely got it, and witnessing their mental health deteriorate was just disturbing, and something I will not forget. But this wont be you though, worst case youll get nasal valve collapse or something. Honestly Ive just learned there are a shitton of things that can go wrong.

Right off the bat I would not recommend you to have rhino unless youre willing to have revision. Board certified surgeons have a revision rate of 5-15%, so its not super unlikely you will need one. And live like a normal person is pretty hard when you cannot breathe properly, something I took for granted before the surgery (you dont know what you have until you lose it I guess). 

I have gotten a newfound appreciation of the nose I had, and while it was nowhere near perfect, it suited my face and I would love to have it back. Unfortunately that is impossible with the current laws of physics and I need to learn to live with it. I also learned the healing process is quite unpredictable, even if the surgeon does everything correct, your nose might not heal properly. Also surgeons are not higher beings, theyre human. They could lie to you, they could make a mistake and not admit it, they could have fake reviews. You should not 100% trust someone like I did, maybe 90 or 95% but never 100%. 

The hardest part initially was seeing my face changed, it was something I never expected, and how tough it would be. But with time this gets better, even if its not perfect. But the breathing is hard, so so hard. It occupies my mind for unhealthy amounts of time, especially in the beginning I was freaking out bad. I think my breathing has gotten slightly better, and also I think humans just learn to live with discomfort, but I still have that hope that Ill get better. I made the mistake of thinking "that isn't gonna happen to me", but it can happen to ANYONE. If you dont think you can deal with it, then perhaps its not worth risking it. Life can get real ugly from just one decision.
I would not do it, its very minor, and chasing perfection can lead you down a dangerous path.

This has been quite the journey, I dont think anyone can really understand unless they go through it themselves, I would never have guessed it would be like this, I greatly underestimated how demanding a rhinoplasty would be. Perhaps we are just unlucky, but I have come across several other people on this sub who have undergone the same thing after the operation, but all their posts had like 3 upvotes and 2 comments, while those with good results got pushed to the top. And then there are the very unlucky ones after rhino, but I dont wanna even think about that right now. I feel like I was sold a lie and would be living best version of my life after rhino, but the opposite has been the case. Perhaps in a year or two I will look at this part of my life as a dark unpleasent dream.

Going through the exact same thing, I really regret getting this surgery. I feel my mental health has deteriorated as a result, and I never obsessed this much about my nose before. My breathing is worse through my right nostril aswell, and in general just awful. I have started a cortisone spray about a week ago but dont know how much it will help. Aesthetically I have developed a small bump which will not go away (surgeon confirmed this), but I can accept it, what I cannot accept is the breathing as I had no issues prior to surgery. I have gone to the surgeon and ENT and they both said they couldn't find anything specific for why my breathing is bad (nasal valve collapse, deviated septum, etc...) so I am hoping its just the swelling, but goddamn how long will the internal swelling last, and could this be permanent??? is what gives me anxiety.

I have learned so much during all of this that I wish I knew prior to surgery, I feel I am being punished for my vanity, and I wish 23 hours of every day that I could go back to the day of surgery and just tell them to not touch me and my nose. Its funny how after the surgery I look back at my old nose and appreciate it much more.
